builds_on: tag-actions (trigger activity, assignment store), nfc-explorer-mvp (406 tests, Detekt gating, ADR 0001)

user_decisions.sound_source: Android's own ringtone picker, TYPE_NOTIFICATION, silent entry shown. No bundled audio.
user_decisions.scope: tag action triggers only. The in-app scan screen keeps ScanHaptics and gains nothing.
user_decisions.failure_case: an assigned tag whose tap fails gets its own toast and its own tone; today it is log-only

key_constraints: Android's NFC discovery beep on a background tap is played by the platform's NfcService before this app is started; FLAG_READER_NO_PLATFORM_SOUNDS only covers foreground reader mode, so there is no app-side way to silence it. It rides the notification volume stream.
both tones default to Silent: the complaint that prompted this feature is that a tap is too loud, so a second sound on by default would make it worse
ActionPerformer.perform is not awaited, so an action failure arrives after the activity has finished; that toast must use the application context on Dispatchers.Main from ApplicationScope
minSdk 26, and Ringtone.setVolume is API 28, so playback is MediaPlayer
domain/ stays framework-free; every android.media and Toast reference lives in data/feedback
no new permission, and specifically not VIBRATE

phases.title: The pure decision
phases.outcome: what a tap should say is decided in framework-free Kotlin and proven by tests

phases.title: Preferences
phases.outcome: four settings persist across restart and reach the settings ViewModel

phases.title: Making the sound and the toast
phases.outcome: an assigned tap announces itself; an unassigned one still does nothing

phases.title: Settings UI
phases.outcome: the four preferences are reachable, and the section says what the app cannot control

phases.title: Docs and device verification
phases.outcome: AC1-AC8 evidenced on hardware, README states what cannot be silenced

notable_decisions: MediaPlayer rather than Ringtone: Ringtone.setVolume is API 28 and minSdk is 26, so the volume slider would silently do nothing on the two oldest supported releases - a setting that appears to work and does not is worse than no setting

SharedPreferences rather than DataStore, unlike the assignment store: these are read synchronously on a tap, on a path that must not suspend before the action fires, and nothing observes them as a flow. Matches PreferencesTogglConfig
not synced to Drive: a tone content URI is device-local and a volume is a property of this phone, so pushing either to another device would be wrong
the toast and the tone are decided by one pure TapFeedback.onDispatch rather than three call sites in the activity, so the announcement cannot drift out of step with the log

the failure reason shown to the user is prose, not the exception, on the presence path - presenceDetail already produces the diagnostic form for the log, and that is a different audience. On the action path the exception IS the useful thing, because an action that fails is a configuration problem the user has to fix
the section subtitle states that the platform beep is not ours. Without it the feature reads as broken the first time a user sets a quiet tone and still hears the loud one
known_tradeoffs: the loud beep the user actually complained about is not fixable from the app; the only lever is the device notification volume, and it is system-wide

no unit test covers AndroidFeedbackAnnouncer or PreferencesFeedbackSettings, consistent with TagActionRunner and DataStoreAssignmentDocuments - the logic worth testing was hoisted into domain/feedback and everything left is adapter
the toast is not rate-limited, so a card tapped repeatedly toasts repeatedly. Suppressing a toast after a real tap is worse than repeating one, and the preference turns it off in one tap
one pair of tones for the whole app rather than per-assignment tones

parallel_execution.note: every phase consumes types the previous one creates, and phase 4 edits the same ViewModel as phase 2

recommended_next_commands: /aw:test  (device verification: a phone, an assigned card and an unassigned one)
validation_commands: ./gradlew :app:detekt  (16 weighted issues, ALL pre-existing - see verification.md)
save_point_commits: feat: decide what a tap should say, in the domain
feat: announce a tap with a tone and a toast
feat: choose the tap sound and toast in settings
fix: a tone whose file has gone no longer reads as Silent
docs: tap feedback verified as far as an emulator can
defects_found_during_build: the first draft put English prose in domain/, contradicting the rule Labels.kt states; replaced with a TapFailure code resolved in the announcer

a refused non-NFC launch would have announced itself, handing an exported activity a toast-spam vector and a way to learn which UIDs are assigned; onDispatch now returns Ignored unless the launch was a genuine dispatch

a tone whose file had been deleted rendered as "Silent", claiming no sound was set when one was. getTitle does not return null for a dead media row - it falls back to the last path segment, so the first fix rendered "38". Fixed by asking whether the URI opens
blockers: AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5 are only partially verified: no NFC in the emulator and no card available, so no tap was ever dispatched. The preview path exercises the same announce() with the same TapOutcome but not TagActionActivity, TagPresence, or the platform dispatch.
the README claims Detekt gating; :app:detekt has been failing on this branch with 16 pre-existing findings since before this feature. Out of scope here.
